cards.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
cards.title_cn: Gilbert + Tobin 用人工智能重新思考法律业务
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】A conversation with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin.
fulltext: November 12, 2026
A conversation with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin.
Our Executive Function series features perspectives from leaders driving transformation through AI.

Gilbert + Tobin⁠(opens in a new window) is one of Australia’s leading corporate law firms, with work spanning capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, disputes, and technology. The firm operates in a profession built on specialist knowledge, careful judgement, and the secure handling of sensitive information.

Gilbert + Tobin began by giving its people room to experiment with AI, then introduced ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Work and Codex to move from individual assistance to defined, multistep agentic workflows, with people responsible for review and approval.
We spoke with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin, about leading adoption from the front, where he’s seeing the value of AI, and his advice for other CEOs.
We have three objectives: to use AI to deliver better services to our clients, make Gilbert + Tobin a great place to work for our people and firmly establish ourselves as a leader in our market.

The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.
“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”

When ChatGPT first became available, we encouraged people to experiment with it and think about where it might create value. We were clear that no client data or confidential information should be entered. That gave people a safe, constrained environment to experiment.

The next step was to provide a secure channel to powerful AI. We introduced ChatGPT Enterprise in a controlled environment and expanded from there. Australian data residency, contractual protections, role-based access and administrative controls gave us the confidence to scale while meeting our requirements and those of our clients.

Governance should enable responsible use. Our message was simple: AI is not cheating. It is another tool people can use to apply their judgement. They still need to define the task, check the output and take responsibility for the final work.
Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm.
Gilbert + Tobin has always been willing to lean into new technology. What has been most encouraging is the creativity coming from every part of the organisation – not only the technology team.
“Getting started yourself…sets the tone and encourages others.”

To help manage my workload more effectively, I created a “digital twin” through a custom GPT (now shifting to Plugins) using examples of my writing, feedback I had received, context about the firm and the way I like to work. It started as a tool for me and became more valuable when I shared it with my direct reports.

My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. It lets them test their thinking against my context and working style before coming to me. It does not make decisions or speak for me; it helps our conversations start from a stronger place.

I also used ChatGPT Work in a confidential annual review process involving our 120 partners. I asked it to update files with data from a spreadsheet, create PDFs and bundle the finished material. It completed the work in minutes.

With a product as powerful as ChatGPT Work, it’s important to have the right admin controls behind the scenes, and it now provides detailed, granular data on usage. When I checked the usage dashboard afterwards, the cost for that annual review work was about $62. That was a good trade for the time I saved – and for work that would otherwise have required several other people over multiple days.
Start by using the technology yourself. Experiment with real work, understand its limitations and show your people that learning matters.
Pair that leadership with clear governance and practical enablement. Give teams examples tailored to their roles, create safe ways to test ideas and keep people responsible for the result.

The opportunity is bigger than doing the same work a little more quickly. Used well, AI can raise the quality and volume of what an organisation produces – and give people more time for the complex, strategic work where their expertise and judgement create the greatest value.
Find out more about Gilbert + Tobin’s work with OpenAI through the case study here.
cards.summary_cn: 【OpenAI】与 Gilbert + Tobin 合伙人兼首席执行官 Sam Nickless 的对话。
fulltext_cn: 与 Gilbert + Tobin 合伙人兼首席执行官 Sam Nickless 的对话。
我们的执行职能系列以领导者通过人工智能推动转型的观点为特色。
Gilbert + Tobin⁠（在新窗口中打开）是澳大利亚领先的公司律师事务所之一，业务范围涵盖资本市场、并购、争议和技术。该公司的业务建立在专业知识、仔细判断和敏感信息安全处理的基础上。
Gilbert + Tobin 首先为员工提供了试验人工智能的空间，然后引入了 ChatGPT Enterprise、ChatGPT Work 和 Codex，从个人协助转向定义的、多步骤的代理工作流程，并由人员负责审查和批准。
我们与 Gilbert + Tobin 合伙人兼首席执行官 Sam Nickless 进行了交谈，讨论了如何从前沿引领采用，他看到了人工智能的价值，以及他对其他首席执行官的建议。
我们有三个目标：利用人工智能为我们的客户提供更好的服务，使 Gilbert + Tobin 成为我们员工的理想工作场所，并牢固树立我们市场领导者的地位。
到目前为止，我们从人工智能中看到的真正价值并不是降低成本或需要更少的人员，而是让我们的员工能够专注于工作中更人性化的一面，与客户会面，指导他们的团队以及指导我们行业的未来领导者。
“这是为了……让他们自由地去做他们的工作中更人性化的一面。”
当 ChatGPT 首次推出时，我们鼓励人们尝试它并思考它可以在哪里创造价值。我们明确表示不应输入任何客户数据或机密信息。这为人们提供了一个安全、受限的实验环境。
下一步是为强大的人工智能提供安全通道。我们在受控环境中引入了 ChatGPT Enterprise，并在此基础上进行了扩展。澳大利亚数据驻留、合同保护、基于角色的访问和管理控制使我们有信心在满足我们和客户的要求的同时进行扩展。
治理应促进负责任的使用。我们的信息很简单：人工智能不会作弊。这是人们可以用来做出判断的另一个工具。他们仍然需要定义任务、检查输出并对最终工作负责。
领导者必须亲自使用该技术：进行实验、突破界限并了解什么是行之有效的。当人们看到人工智能对你很重要时，它就会定下基调并鼓励其他人参与其中。
我们没有强制规定使用目标。相反，我们使技术具有相关性。我们的业务转型团队展示了针对不同职能定制的工作流程，同时视频、展示、挑战和早期人工智能赏金浮现了整个公司的想法。
Gilbert + Tobin 始终愿意尝试新技术。最令人鼓舞的是来自组织各个部分的创造力——而不仅仅是技术团队。
“你自己开始……定下基调并鼓励他人。”
为了帮助更有效地管理我的工作量，我通过自定义 GPT（现在转向插件）使用我的写作示例、收到的反馈、公司背景以及我喜欢的工作方式创建了一个“数字孪生”。它最初是我的一个工具，当我与我的直接下属分享它时，它变得更有价值。
我的团队现在可以使用它通过 ChatGPT 有效地获取“我的反馈”。这让他们可以在来找我之前根据我的背景和工作风格测试他们的想法。它不代表我做决定或说话；它帮助我们的对话从更强有力的地方开始。
我还在涉及我们 120 个合作伙伴的保密年度审查流程中使用了 ChatGPT Work。我要求它使用电子表格中的数据更新文件、创建 PDF 并捆绑完成的材料。它在几分钟内完成了工作。
对于像 ChatGPT Work 这样强大的产品，在幕后拥有正确的管理控制非常重要，它现在提供详细、精细的使用数据。当我事后检查使用情况仪表板时，年度审核工作的成本约为 62 美元。对于我节省的时间来说，这是一笔很好的交易，而且对于原本需要其他几个人花几天时间完成的工作来说也是一笔不错的交易。
从自己使用该技术开始。尝试实际工作，了解其局限性并向员工表明学习很重要。
将这种领导力与明确的治理和实际的支持相结合。为团队提供适合其角色的示例，创建安全的方法来测试想法并使人们对结果负责。
机会比更快地完成同样的工作更大。如果运用得当，人工智能可以提高组织产品的质量和数量，并让人们有更多的时间从事复杂的战略性工作，在这些工作中，他们的专业知识和判断力可以创造最大的价值。
通过此处的案例研究了解更多有关 Gilbert + Tobin 与 OpenAI 合作的信息。

The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to a scramble for electricity. Before those challenges even come into play, though, there’s a more basic problem: A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. With billions of dollars in AI infrastructure investment at stake, separating realistic projects from speculative ones is becoming increasingly important.

On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, hosts Rebecca Bellan and Tim De Chant are joined by Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics, to separate the data center projects that are likely to get built from the ones that may never get off the ground.
Audio Producer

Theresa Loconsolo is an audio producer at TechCrunch focusing on Equity, the network’s flagship podcast. Before joining TechCrunch in 2022, she was one of 2 producers at a four-station conglomerate where she wrote, recorded, voiced and edited content, and engineered live performances and interviews from guests like lovelytheband. Theresa is based in New Jersey and holds a bachelors degree in Communication from Monmouth University.
You can contact or verify outreach from Theresa by emailing [email protected].
Senior Reporter

Rebecca Bellan is a senior reporter at TechCrunch where she covers the business, policy, and emerging trends shaping artificial intelligence. Her work has also appeared in Forbes, Bloomberg, The Atlantic, The Daily Beast, and other publications.
You can contact or verify outreach from Rebecca by emailing [email protected] or via encrypted message at rebeccabellan.491 on Signal.
Senior Reporter, Climate

Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.
You can contact or verify outreach from Tim by emailing [email protected].

cards.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
cards.title_cn: CoreWeave 转向客户预付款和较短的合同来为人工智能的发展提供资金
cards.summary: 【TechCrunch】CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay upfront, borrowing against specific contracts, and even looking to short-term deals that could lead to higher prices, according to the company’s third…

CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.

The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.
CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.
“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.

Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.

CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.
Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts.

Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge.
CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices.

The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator.

“We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said.

CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.

While short-term deals let CoreWeave charge higher prices and change them more frequently, it’s a tradeoff. Lenders give more weight to longer-term contracts, even if they’re priced lower, because they value predictable cash flow and consistency to repay the loan above all.

Even though Wall Street reacted positively to CoreWeave’s earnings, bond investors are much less sanguine. Last month, yields on some of the company’s bonds hit above 15%, highlighting that investors are concerned about the debt needed to fund data center buildouts before those investments see a return.

In short, CoreWeave is finding new ways to expand without relying on unsecured debt. The strategy it has chosen could boost profits, but it also carries greater risk around contract renewals and pricing — and it just goes to show how dependent the AI infrastructure boom is on sustained, and as yet unproven, demand.
TechCrunch has reached out to CoreWeave for more information about its loan facility.

根据周二公布的第三季度财报，CoreWeave 正在重写其为人工智能热潮付出代价的方式。 CoreWeave 是一家出租人工智能背后计算能力的新云公司，该公司表示，它越来越多地要求客户预先付款、根据特定合同借款，甚至寻求可能导致价格上涨的短期交易。
新战略可以帮助 CoreWeave 更有效地为其增长提供资金，同时从现有基础设施中榨取更多现金。但只有当前的需求和定价能力持续下去，这些赌注才会成立。
CoreWeave 公布的收入为 36.6 亿美元，较上年增长 168%，但也公布了 7.09 亿美元的净亏损和 8.46 亿美元的季度利息支出。
CoreWeave 首席执行官 Michael Intrator 在周二的财报电话会议上表示：“我们不会也没有必要利用无担保债务市场以当前的收益率为我们的业务提供资金。”
相反，CoreWeave 的计划是依靠特定客户合同支持的贷款，根据需要动用资金来为其仍需建设的大部分基础设施提供资金，以交付 1,325 亿美元的大量积压订单。
CoreWeave还表示，预计未来三个月将获得约90亿美元的客户预付款和押金，其中包括超过30亿美元用于为其已建设的产能签署新客户合同，这不需要额外的硬件支出。
竞争对手 Nebius 和 IREN 也依赖微软的巨额预付款来支付计算能力，这表明该行业正朝着要求大型科技公司支付其扩建费用的方向发展。
预付款可以缓解 CoreWeave 的即时借贷需求，但也承诺该公司提供服务的价格可能会随着计算需求的持续激增而降低吸引力。
CoreWeave 还希望通过签署更多可以提高价格的短期合同来利用不断增长的需求。
该公司 7 月份将其产品价格提高了约 25%，并在本季度晚些时候又提高了 10%。 Intrator 表示，本季度价格仍在攀升，“足以抵消成本上涨”。
这位首席执行官表示：“我们还将更多产能分配给短期机会，价格合理，每年销售产能超过每兆瓦 4000 万美元，而四年期和五年期合同的新基础设施定价则升至每兆瓦 2000 万至 2500 万美元。”
CoreWeave 的融资策略现在围绕着这些机会。 8 月，该公司完成了一笔 26 亿美元的贷款，这是第一笔专门针对短期客户合同的贷款。它被称为 DDTL 5.5，它允许 CoreWeave 在需要资金时分期借款。
虽然短期交易让 CoreWeave 收取更高的价格并更频繁地更改价格，但这是一种权衡。贷款人更重视长期合同，即使价格较低，因为他们最看重的是可预测的现金流和偿还贷款的一致性。
尽管华尔街对 CoreWeave 的收益反应积极，但债券投资者却远没有那么乐观。上个月，该公司部分债券的收益率达到 15% 以上，突显出投资者对在这些投资获得回报之前为数据中心建设提供资金所需的债务感到担忧。
简而言之，CoreWeave 正在寻找新的扩张方式，而不依赖无担保债务。它选择的策略可以提高利润，但也带来了合同续签和定价方面的更大风险——这恰恰表明人工智能基础设施的繁荣对持续的、尚未得到证实的需求有多么依赖。
TechCrunch 已联系 CoreWeave，了解有关其贷款安排的更多信息。

cards.title: Google brings the standalone Gemini app and Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay
cards.title_cn: 谷歌将独立的 Gemini 应用程序和 Gemini Live 引入 Apple CarPlay
cards.summary: 【Google】TL;DR Google is rolling out a standalone Gemini app to Apple CarPlay globally, bringing Gemini Live to the platform. Unlike its existing Google Maps integration, the standalone app supports broader co…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Google is expanding its AI presence on Apple CarPlay by bringing the standalone Gemini app to the platform starting today, Wednesday, November 11. For reference, CarPlay users have already been able to leverage Gemini’s smarts, albeit only in Maps. The development today takes things a step further.

The new standalone app brings access to Gemini Live too, unlocking hands-free conversational assistance throughout your rides. The move has been a long time coming, especially considering that AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Copilot are already available on CarPlay.

Compared to the existing implementation via Google Maps, the standalone Gemini app opens the door to a much broader range of use cases. For starters, the assistant retains context. According to Google, when you tap the Gemini app icon on your CarPlay screen, you’ll essentially pick up right where you left off with a recent chat.

Additionally, Gemini syncs across devices too, so every conversation you have with either device will be available to pick up on the other. You’ll be able to start a Gemini conversation on your iPhone while leaving home, continue it during your drive, and return to it on your phone once you’ve reached your destination.

It’s worth noting that the integration doesn’t give Gemini deep device-level permissions, so don’t expect it to change music, adjust the AC, or control other CarPlay apps. Instead, the focus here is on conversational assistance.

Gemini’s Workspace integration means that the app can connect to apps like Gmail and Google Calendar and give you a Daily Brief of your day during your morning commute. It can also conversationally help you “catch up on unread emails, get quick summaries of long email threads, and talk through a quick reply using just your voice.”

Beyond giving you a rundown of your day, Gemini Live, just like its implementation on your phone, can help you brainstorm ideas, help rehearse an upcoming presentation, discuss a topic you’ve been curious about, and more. The tool’s conversational nature means you can interrupt it, ask follow-up questions, or guide the conversation into a different topic without having to start a new chat. If you use Gemini Live on your phone, it won’t take you long to get accustomed to the CarPlay Gemini Live experience.

The standalone app is rolling out globally to all Gemini users on iOS across every supported Gemini Live language. You don’t need a separate application — just ensure that the Gemini app on your iPhone is updated to the latest version and that you’ve used Gemini Live on your phone at least once. Note that I haven’t received a Gemini app update yet, and I don’t have the app on CarPlay just yet. Given that the rollout has only begun today, it could take a few days for the app to show up for everyone.
Once available, simply tapping the Gemini app icon on your CarPlay dashboard should let you jump straight into a conversation or pick up where you left off.

除了为您提供一天的概要之外，Gemini Live 就像它在手机上的实现一样，还可以帮助您集思广益，帮助排练即将进行的演示，讨论您一直好奇的主题等等。该工具的对话性质意味着您可以打断它、提出后续问题或将对话引导到不同的主题，而无需开始新的聊天。如果您在手机上使用 Gemini Live，那么您很快就会习惯 CarPlay Gemini Live 体验。

Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.

Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.
However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.

As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.

Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual tradeoff between memory and capacity.

This tradeoff has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.

In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

英国政府表示，开发人工智能芯片的初创公司 Fractile 已筹集了 7.2 亿美元的 C 轮融资，由英国主权人工智能基金支持，希望“确保英国在支撑其未来经济的硬件中拥有更大的股份”。
这使得 Fractile 与 Axelera、Etched 和 OLIX 等公司一起，成为专用 AI 芯片竞赛中资金最多的初创公司之一。此类芯片是正在探索的降低推理成本的几种途径之一——也就是在生产中使用要求越来越高的人工智能模型。
然而，Fractile 寻求超越硬件的全栈方法，其中还包括机器学习编译器，以最大限度地提高 LLM 在其芯片上的执行速度。
因此，该公司将自己定位为一家前沿人工智能公司，由 Thrive Capital、Founders Fund、Lightspeed Venture Partners 和 Redpoint 领投的最新一轮融资也相应定价。据英国政府称，该估值“超过 50 亿英镑”——很可能是 70 亿美元，英国《金融时报》和路透社消息人士均报道了这一数字。
尽管如此，Fractile 的主要区别可以说是它的硬件设计。经过一次转型后，它的方法现在以 DRAM（最常见的 RAM 类型）为中心，但以这样的方式堆叠在每个芯片的顶部，希望能够绕过内存和容量之间的通常权衡。
随着代理人工智能的兴起，这种权衡变​​得更加成问题，因为公司寻求在不影响速度的情况下使用大型模型执行更长的任务链。由于计算能力难以跟上，人们对人工智能芯片寄予厚望，尽管迄今为止它们的可用性有限。
Fractile 首席执行官沃尔特·古德温 (Walter Goodwin) 在 LinkedIn 的一篇帖子中写道，该公司“还有很多工作要做”，新的资金将使这家初创公司能够“明年推出第一批芯片和系统”。

cards.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
cards.title_cn: Gemini Decisions API：快速、经过校准的多模式决策
cards.summary: 【Google】Meet the Gemini Decisions API, powered by our state-of-the-art model Gemini Decision for fast, calibrated multimodal decisions.
fulltext: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

The Decisions API gives you purpose-built primitives for bounded choices like tool selection, policy checks, model routing, and context grading. You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions. Rather than generating answer text token by token, Gemini Decision 1 scores your candidate options in a single forward pass, returning probabilities and confidence scores in 150-250 ms end-to-end latency at $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed.
On benchmarks spanning agent routing, reasoning, ranking, and multimodal understanding, Gemini Decision 1 leads across the suite, with the lowest calibration error.

Gemini Decision 1 scores options without token-by-token decoding, keeping median latency 50-100 ms of model compute (150-250 ms end-to-end), across multimodal inputs and contexts up to 16K tokens, remaining nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request. With zero output tokens billed, Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API.

Built on Gemini’s native multimodal architecture, Gemini Decision 1 can process text, images, audio, video, and PDFs directly in a single forward pass. You can combine modalities in one shared input, such as pairing a call recording with account metadata or a scanned PDF claim with damage photos, and tune resolution on image and video inputs to control visual detail and token cost.

You can evaluate multiple questions against that shared input in a single request, mixing yes/no checks, multiple choice, and rubric scores. Every answer includes a confidence score (from 0 to 1) so your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer:

The input field uses the same Content block format as the Interactions API. Here is how to check a photo of a breakroom counter, together with a text note, against all three question types in one request:

Teams across Google are already using the Decisions API as a low-latency control plane, shipping features simply by defining options rather than training custom classifiers or waiting on generative calls:
Stitch Rapid uses the Decisions API to design an entire product flow in seconds (1x speed).

Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens, with an API no-cost tier you can use in Google AI Studio for prototyping. Your shared input is billed once per request no matter how many questions you evaluate (each question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens). There are no output-token charges, variable thinking-token bills, or separate audio transcription and OCR costs.

You can start building today by grabbing an API key in Google AI Studio, trying our Doorstep Parcels, Speed Sketch, and Find the Zoo Keeper demo apps, and following the Python, JavaScript, and REST guides in the Decisions API documentation.

Ecosystem integrations are rolling out across OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit, and OpenCode alongside the google-genai SDKs, with support coming soon to Gemini in Google Cloud.

cards.summary_cn: 【Google】了解 Gemini Decisions API，它由我们最先进的模型 Gemini Decision 提供支持，可实现快速、校准的多模式决策。
fulltext_cn: 今天，我们将推出 Gemini Decisions API，这是一个新的端点，用于快速、闭集决策，由我们的新 Gemini Decision 1 模型 (gemini-decision-1) 提供支持，可通过 Google AI Studio 中的 Gemini API 获取。

Decisions API 为您提供了专门构建的原语，用于有界选择，例如工具选择、策略检查、模型路由和上下文分级。您可以跨文本、图像、音频、视频和 PDF（最多 256K 个标记）传递一个多模式输入以及最多 1,000 个独立问题。 Gemini Decision 1 不是按令牌生成答案文本令牌，而是在一次前向传递中对候选选项进行评分，以每 100 万个输入令牌 0.10 美元的价格在 150-250 毫秒的端到端延迟内返回概率和置信度分数，输出令牌计费为零。
在涵盖代理路由、推理、排名和多模式理解的基准测试中，Gemini Decision 1 在整个套件中处于领先地位，并且校准误差最低。

Gemini Decision 1 对选项进行评分，无需逐个令牌解码，在多模式输入和多达 16K 个令牌的上下文中，模型计算的中值延迟保持在 50-100 毫秒（端到端 150-250 毫秒），每个请求 1 到 100 个问题几乎保持不变。由于输出代币为零，带有决策 API 的 Gemini Decision 1 在整个共享基准套件中的价格比带有交互 API 的 Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 便宜近 5 倍。
Gemini Decision 1 基于 Gemini 的本机多模式架构构建，可以在一次前向传递中直接处理文本、图像、音频、视频和 PDF。您可以将各种模式组合到一个共享输入中，例如将通话录音与帐户元数据配对，或将扫描的 PDF 索赔与损坏照片配对，并调整图像和视频输入的分辨率以控制视觉细节和令牌成本。
您可以在单个请求中针对共享输入评估多个问题，混合是/否检查、多项选择和评分标准。每个答案都包含一个置信度分数（从 0 到 1），因此您的代码可以将不明确的案例路由给后备或人工审阅者：
输入字段使用与交互 API 相同的内容块格式。以下是如何根据一个请求中的所有三种问题类型检查休息室柜台的照片以及文本注释：
Google 的团队已经在使用 Decisions API 作为低延迟控制平面，只需定义选项即可提供功能，而不是训练自定义分类器或等待生成调用：
Stitch Rapid 使用 Decisions API 在几秒钟内设计出整个产品流程（1 倍速度）。
Gemini Decision 1 的定价为每 100 万个输入代币 0.10 美元，输出代币为 0 美元，您可以在 Google AI Studio 中使用 API 免费层进行原型设计。无论您评估多少问题，您的共享输入都会按请求计费一次（每个问题仅添加自己的说明和标准标记）。没有输出令牌费用、可变思维令牌账单或单独的音频转录和 OCR 成本。
您可以立即开始构建，方法是在 Google AI Studio 中获取 API 密钥，尝试我们的 Doorstep Parcels、Speed Sketch 和 Find the Zoo Keeper 演示应用程序，并遵循 Decisions API 文档中的 Python、JavaScript 和 REST 指南。
生态系统集成正在 OpenRouter、LangChain、Vercel、LiteLLM、Pydantic AI、Pipecat、LiveKit 和 OpenCode 以及 google-genai SDK 上推出，并且很快将支持 Google Cloud 中的 Gemini。

cards.title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
cards.title_cn: 尝试桌面：可定制的协作空间，供团队一起计划、玩耍和做更多事情。
cards.summary: 【Google】Tabletop is a new Google Labs experiment for group collaboration. Build interactive itineraries, polls, and brackets with your team. Join the waitlist.
fulltext: Whether you’re planning a family trip, running a rec league or hosting a potluck, coordinating as a group is easier when everyone can pitch in, build and decide together in one place.
Today, we’re introducing Tabletop, a new Google Labs experiment built for real-time collaboration.

Just add in your links, files, and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets. Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time, like in a Google Doc.
Tabletop is rolling out in the U.S. (18+) via waitlist. Pull up a chair and sign up at labs.google/tabletop.
cards.summary_cn: 【Google】Tabletop 是 Google 实验室针对团队协作进行的一项新实验。与您的团队建立互动行程、民意调查和分组。加入候补名单。
fulltext_cn: 无论您是计划家庭旅行、举办休闲联赛还是举办聚餐，当每个人都可以在一个地方共同参与、建设和决策时，团队协调就会变得更加容易。
今天，我们要介绍 Tabletop，这是一项专为实时协作而构建的新 Google 实验室实验。
只需添加您的链接、文件和想法，然后提示@tabletop - 或选择一个入门模板 - 即可生成自定义交互式旅行行程、晚餐民意调查、费用分配器和锦标赛分组。一旦您的空间准备就绪，请将邀请链接放入群聊中，以便每个人都可以同时加入并使用它，就像在 Google 文档中一样。
Tabletop 正在美国（18 岁以上）通过候补名单推出。拉出一把椅子并在 labs.google/tabletop 上注册。

cards.summary: 【Android Authority】Big screens are great for getting more done on your phone, but most handsets still feel cramped when you’re juggling apps, reading documents, or watching video. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is bu…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Big screens are great for getting more done on your phone, but most handsets still feel cramped when you’re juggling apps, reading documents, or watching video. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is built for that kind of heavy daily use, and there’s a solid deal on it right now on Amazon.

The unlocked Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra in Graphite is down to $2,048.39, from its $2,299.99 recommended retail price. That’s an 11% discount off the RRP, which works out to about $251 in savings. This isn’t a record low, but it is close to its lowest price. It’s also worth noting that this deal is for the Graphite color, while Violet is still listed at $2,299.99.

This version comes with 512GB of storage and 16GB of RAM, so it’s aimed at buyers who want lots of room for apps, photos, videos, and large files, along with strong performance for multitasking. Samsung pairs that with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 chip and a foldable design centered around a large inner display. Both screens support a 120Hz refresh rate, and the cover screen is large enough to use regular Android apps comfortably without opening the phone.

Camera hardware includes dual 50MP main cameras and a 50MP selfie camera. You also get a display brightness claim of up to 4,500 nits, plus battery life aimed at all-day flagship use. If you’ve been looking for a premium foldable that can handle work, media, and everyday phone tasks in one device, this Amazon deal makes the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra a bit easier to justify. It also has a 4.6-star Amazon rating.
